summary: Issue creation validates domain values and team-owned references before reserving numbers; counter overflow and rejected mutators preserve prior state.
Explicit stale versions and real PostgreSQL xmin save conflicts produce typed HTTP 409, while unexpected exception details are hidden behind generic HTTP 500 responses.

Production EF mapping ignores duplicate public collection views and declares domain-generated IDs, fixing model startup and insertion of newly appended activity records while retaining xmin and team/key uniqueness.
Notification events clear only after successful enqueue; tests demonstrate that enqueue failure after commit retains the event but is not durable delivery.
All 14 .NET tests pass against a disposable PostgreSQL server, including actual two-context concurrency and API health. The React TypeScript/Vite production build passes.
Nine rewritten source-based learning guides, a PostgreSQL test helper, exact before snapshots and portable verification evidence are included.

checks.command: Recorded complete suite and build/type checks

limits: Notification delivery remains in memory after commit; crash loss and partial-enqueue duplication require a future durable outbox.
The health smoke test and direct mapper tests do not constitute complete authenticated browser end-to-end coverage.
Existing development login, demonstration seed identities and future product backlog remain as documented in the project README.
